questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Indonesia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Indonesia article.

questions.proof: The capital of Indonesia is Jakarta, on the island of Java, but there are plans to change it to Nusantara.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Indonesia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Indonesia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Indonesia article.

questions.proof: Indonesia's neighbors are Australia to the south, Singapore to the northwest, and Philippines to the northeast.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Indonesia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Indonesia article.

questions.proof: The official national language of Indonesia is Indonesian, but 749 native languages are also spoken in various parts of Indonesia, and native languages widely spoken in Indonesia include Javanese, Balinese, and Sundanese.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Other nearby countries are Papua New _____, Malaysia, and East Timor which share land borders with Indonesia.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Malaysia”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Indonesia article.

questions.proof: Other nearby countries are Papua New Guinea, Malaysia, and East Timor which share land borders with Indonesia.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The land area is 1,904,000 square kilometres (735,000 sq mi), or slightly smaller than _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “smaller”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Indonesia article.
